cards.text: Every tribe in Israel has its land now, except the Levites, whose share is the priesthood of the LORD instead of a chunk of land (Joshua 18:7; 19:51). So at Shiloh, the Levite family heads walk up to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, Israel's leader, and the heads of the other tribes. It's like everybody's already walked off with their slice of the dough, and one friend holds up the recipe card: "Uh, friends? It says here we get some too."

cards.question: The Levite leaders say the LORD gave a command about them. Who did the LORD give that command through?
The Levites have no land of their own. What does the LORD's command say they should be given?

answers.text: A share of the war spoils

cards.question: Along with the cities, the Levites ask for ___ for their livestock.
So how do the tribes of Israel answer the Levites' request for cities?

answers.text: They give cities out of their own land
They tell the Levites to wait a year
They point them to land not yet conquered

cards.text: The cities are handed out by lot, clan by clan, to the families of Levi's sons Kohath, Gershon and Merari (Exodus 6:16), and the first lot comes out for the Kohathites, starting with Aaron's descendants, the priests. The priests get Hebron, though its fields and villages had already gone to Caleb son of Jephunneh, one of the twelve spies sent by Moses, Israel's leader before Joshua (Numbers 13:6). Cities of refuge, like Hebron and Shechem, are on the list too. Forty-eight cities in all, from the other tribes' land, and every one of them has its own pasturelands.
Then comes the big picture: the land the LORD swore to give Israel's fathers. I step back to admire my sealed cookie boxes too, and EVERY single time, my mustache knocks one off the counter.

cards.question: How much of the land He swore to Israel's fathers does the LORD give Israel?
Once the LORD gives Israel the land, they take possession of it and settle in it.
With none of their enemies able to stand against them, the LORD gives Israel ___ on every side, just as He swore to their fathers.
None of Israel's enemies can stand against them. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD handed them all over to Israel
Israel's army had grown too big to beat
Their enemies had all fled the land

cards.question: A few of the LORD's good promises to the house of Israel had failed.
